summary: Page 8 of the Daily Inter Mountain (Butte, Montana), dated Thursday, August 2, 1894, is a densely packed interior page mixing local news, city council reporting, health statistics, racing results, and a heavy load of commercial advertising. The left two columns are dominated by local political and civic news, including the mayor's opposition to riot-bill payments and a city council report. The centre columns carry Butte's health report with July mortality statistics, a weather summary, a detailed account of running races at the Smelter grounds, a notice on army ballooning, and a Swedish community meeting notice. The right half of the page is almost entirely advertising — shoe retailers, druggists, coal merchants, flour brands, furniture, sign-painting, and clothing — with large display type competing for the eye. The editorial tone throughout the news columns is matter-of-fact and local in focus, with no sensational treatment even of the riot-bill controversy.
headlines: Five Deaths From Gunshot Wounds Dur-ing July.

clipping_placements.placement_note: Top of col 2, directly under the page dateline banner; largest news headline on the page's left half

juxtapositions: The mayor's report on riot-bill payments and civic disorder sits immediately adjacent in col 1 to a Gans & Klein clothing advertisement urging readers to 'Replenish Your Ties' at 25c — the juxtaposition of civic unrest and retail gentility is striking.

The Butte Health Report noting five gunshot-wound deaths in July — explicitly tied to 'the unfortunate riot on the Fourth' — runs one column over from a large shoe advertisement asking 'DO YOUR FEET HURT?' with an illustration of a boot.
